content.text: {"predictors": [{"name": "Inventory Growth Divergence", "construction": "Compute year-over-year growth in inventories (Compustat item INVT) minus year-over-year growth in sales (item SALE), using the most recent fiscal year annual data. Rank stocks cross-sectionally into deciles each June.", "rationale": "When inventories build faster than sales, it signals weakening demand and future markdowns/write-offs, which the market underweights; firms depleting inventory relative to sales are experiencing stronger-than-expected demand.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (inventory growing slower than sales)"}, {"name": "Accrual-Adjusted Earnings Quality", "construction": "For each firm compute total accruals as the change in non-cash current assets minus change in current liabilities (excluding short-term debt) minus depreciation, scaled by average total assets (Compustat items ACT, CHE, LCT, DLC, DP, AT). Sort into deciles annually.", "rationale": "Earnings driven by accruals rather than cash flows are less persistent and tend to reverse, so the market overprices high-accrual firms.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (low accruals)"}, {"name": "R&D Intensity Relative to Market Cap", "construction": "Compute research and development expense (Compustat item XRD) divided by end-of-year market capitalization (PRCC_F times CSHO). Set missing XRD to zero. Rank into deciles each June.", "rationale": "R&D creates intangible capital that GAAP expenses immediately, causing systematic undervaluation of research-intensive firms whose future payoffs are not yet in book value.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (high R&D relative to market value)"}, {"name": "Gross Profitability Yield", "construction": "Compute gross profit (Compustat item SALE minus COGS) divided by total assets (item AT), using most recent fiscal year. Sort into deciles annually and hold from June.", "rationale": "Gross profits are a cleaner measure of economic productivity than net income because they are less contaminated by accounting/financing noise; more productive firms earn higher returns for their risk.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (high gross profitability)"}, {"name": "Asset Growth Reversal", "construction": "Compute the annual percentage change in total assets (Compustat item AT year over year). Rank all firms into deciles each June.", "rationale": "Rapid asset expansion often reflects overinvestment and empire-building that destroys value and is later corrected; conservatively growing firms outperform.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (low asset growth)"}, {"name": "Net External Financing", "construction": "Sum net equity issuance (change in split-adjusted shares outstanding times price, or Compustat SSTK minus PRSTKC) and net debt issuance (change in total debt DLTT+DLC) over the prior fiscal year, scaled by average total assets. Sort into deciles annually.", "rationale": "Managers issue securities when their firm is overvalued and retire them when undervalued, so heavy external financing predicts low future returns.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (net repurchasers/debt retirers)"}, {"name": "Order-Backlog to Sales", "construction": "For firms reporting order backlog (Compustat item OB), compute backlog divided by annual sales (item SALE). Rank reporting firms into quintiles annually.", "rationale": "A large order backlog relative to current sales is a leading indicator of future revenue growth that the market underappreciates when it is buried in footnotes.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (large backlog relative to sales)"}, {"name": "Volatility of Monthly Returns", "construction": "Compute the standard deviation of a stock's monthly returns (CRSP) over the trailing 36 months. Sort into deciles each month and hold value-weighted portfolios.", "rationale": "Idiosyncratically volatile, lottery-like stocks are overbought by underdiversified retail investors, leading to lower subsequent returns despite higher risk.", "higher_returns_for": "low values of the measure (low return volatility)"}, {"name": "Dividend Initiation Momentum", "construction": "Flag firms that initiated or increased cash dividends per share (Compustat DVPSX or CRSP distribution codes) within the trailing 12 months versus those that cut/omitted. Form long-initiators, short-cutters portfolio, rebalanced monthly.", "rationale": "Dividend changes credibly signal management's private information about sustainable future cash flows, and the market underreacts to this signal.", "higher_returns_for": "dividend initiators/increasers (versus cutters)"}, {"name": "Capital Turnover Efficiency", "construction": "Compute sales (Compustat SALE) divided by net property, plant and equipment (item PPENT), using most recent annual data. Sort into deciles each June, controlling within industry.", "rationale": "Firms that generate more sales per dollar of fixed capital use assets more efficiently and convert investment into cash flow faster, a quality dimension the market prices slowly.", "higher_returns_for": "high values of the measure (high capital turnover)"}]}
